expectation: Na/K-ATPase is a basolateral plasma-membrane marker. It should show chicken-wire membrane rings on epithelial cells, with strong lateral staining in glands and crypts. Stroma and lumen should be dark, and the nuclei unstained.
observed: A shows yellow signal confined to the folded epithelium, with glandular and crypt profiles outlined and the surrounding space dark. B shows honeycomb membrane rings, and C shows lateral and basolateral membranes of columnar cells lining a lumen. D shows crisp lateral membranes that avoid the nuclei.
why: The stain is a specific membrane-ring pattern on epithelial cells and follows the glandular architecture, as expected for Na/K-ATPase.
notes: Yellow signal outlines individual epithelial cell membranes in a honeycomb pattern and lines glands and lumens. Non-epithelial areas and nuclei are dark. Compartment, cell type and tissue architecture all match a working Na/K-ATPase stain.
